outcomes.text: Define movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition as characteristics of living organisms.
Compare plant, animal and bacterial cells; identify and explain structures, cell organisation, cell division and specialised-cell functions.
Use magnification equals image size divided by actual size; calculate specimen dimensions and convert millimetres to micrometres.

units.title: B3 Movement into and out of cells

outcomes.text: Explain diffusion, its role in gas and solute movement, and how surface area, temperature, concentration gradient and distance affect it.
Explain osmosis, investigate concentration effects on plant tissues, and relate turgidity, plasmolysis, water potential and organismal water balance.
Explain active transport against concentration gradients using respiratory energy, including uptake of ions by root hairs.
Identify elements in carbohydrates, fats and proteins; describe their molecular building blocks and perform standard tests for starch, sugars, proteins and lipids.
Explain enzymes as specific protein catalysts, including active sites, enzyme–substrate complexes, and effects of temperature and pH.
Explain photosynthesis, its word and balanced equations, chlorophyll’s role, carbohydrate uses, mineral requirements, and factors affecting its rate.
Identify leaf structures and explain how leaf size, thinness and internal features adapt leaves for photosynthesis.
Describe a balanced diet, sources and roles of nutrients, and vitamin-deficiency causes of scurvy and rickets.
Identify digestive organs and explain ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion in relation to their functions.
Distinguish physical and chemical digestion; explain enzyme, hydrochloric-acid and bile functions, including emulsification and suitable pH.
State xylem and phloem functions and identify their positions in roots, stems and leaves.
Identify root hair cells, explain their role and surface-area advantage, and describe water’s pathway through roots, stems and leaves.
Explain transpiration and wilting; investigate and predict effects of temperature, wind speed and humidity on transpiration rate.
Explain phloem translocation of sucrose and amino acids from sources, which release them, to sinks, which use or store them.
Describe circulatory systems, fish single circulation, mammalian double circulation and the advantages of double circulation.
Identify heart structures; explain cardiac contraction, valves, blood direction, monitoring methods, exercise effects, coronary disease risks and prevention.
Describe artery, vein and capillary structure, including wall thickness, lumen diameter and valves in veins.
List red cells, white cells, platelets and plasma as the components of blood.
Define a pathogen as an organism that causes disease.
Identify the main breathing-system structures and their associated capillaries.
State energy uses including muscle contraction, synthesis, division, growth, nerve impulses and temperature maintenance.
State that electrical impulses travel along neurones.
Define a hormone as a gland-produced chemical carried in blood to alter target-organ activity.
Define homeostasis as maintaining a constant internal environment.
Define a drug as a substance that alters chemical reactions in the body.
Describe asexual reproduction as producing genetically identical offspring from one parent.
Describe sexual reproduction as gamete-nucleus fusion producing genetically different offspring.
Identify and draw the specified parts of an insect-pollinated flower.
Identify male reproductive structures and state their functions.
Define an STI as an infection transmitted through sexual contact.
State that DNA in chromosomes carries genetic information as genes.
Describe mitosis as nuclear division producing genetically identical cells.
Understand inheritance, genotypes, phenotypes, homozygous and heterozygous conditions, dominance, pedigrees, monohybrid crosses, phenotypic ratios and Punnett squares.
Describe variation, continuous and discontinuous phenotypes, mutations and mutation’s role in producing new alleles.
Explain natural selection, selective breeding, artificial selection across generations and antibiotic resistance in bacteria.
Recognise the Sun as the main energy source and describe energy transfer through organisms to the environment.

topics.title: B18.2 Food chains and food webs

subtopics.title: B18.2 Food chains and food webs

outcomes.text: Construct and interpret food chains and webs, classify organisms and trophic levels, and explain energy losses and human impacts.
Describe carbon movement through photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, fossil-fuel formation and combustion.
Define ecosystems and biodiversity, explain habitat destruction and deforestation, and identify resulting ecological and atmospheric effects.
Explain causes of endangerment or extinction and describe conservation through protection, education, captive breeding and seed banks.
Compare states of matter, particle arrangements and motion, state changes, heating curves, and temperature or pressure effects on gas volume.
Explain diffusion using kinetic particle theory and relate gas diffusion rates to relative molecular masses.
Distinguish elements, compounds and mixtures.

topics.title: C2.2 Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

subtopics.title: C2.2 Atomic structure and the Periodic Table

outcomes.text: Describe atomic structure, particle charges and masses, proton and mass numbers, electron configurations, and relationships between groups, periods and shells.
Define isotopes, interpret atom and ion symbols, and explain why isotopes have identical chemical properties.
Describe ions, ionic bonding, ionic lattices, dot-and-cross diagrams and ionic compound properties using structure and bonding.

topics.title: C2.5 Simple molecules and covalent bonds

subtopics.title: C2.5 Simple molecules and covalent bonds

outcomes.text: Describe covalent bonding and simple molecular structures, diagrams and properties, including weak intermolecular forces and poor conductivity.
Describe graphite and diamond structures and connect their bonding and properties with specified uses.
Describe metallic bonding and explain metals’ electrical conductivity and malleability from their structure.
State and deduce formulas, construct word and symbol equations, balance equations, include state symbols and derive ionic equations.

topics.title: C3.2 Relative masses of atoms and molecules

subtopics.title: C3.2 Relative masses of atoms and molecules

outcomes.text: Define relative atomic, molecular and formula masses, and calculate reacting masses using simple proportions.

topics.title: C3.3 The mole and the Avogadro constant

subtopics.title: C3.3 The mole and the Avogadro constant

outcomes.text: Use concentration, mole, Avogadro constant, molar-mass and gas-volume relationships to calculate amounts, masses, volumes and limiting reactants.
Understand electrolysis, identify electrodes and electrolyte, predict products, explain charge transfer, and write cathode reduction half-equations.
Explain how hydrogen–oxygen fuel cells generate electricity with water as the only product, including advantages and disadvantages compared with petrol engines.
Distinguish exothermic and endothermic reactions, interpret and draw energy diagrams, define enthalpy and activation energy, and relate energy changes to bonds.
Identify physical and chemical changes and explain how they differ.
Explain and investigate how concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts affect reaction rates using collision theory and data.
Define redox, oxidation and reduction using oxygen, electrons and oxidation numbers, and identify these processes in reactions.

topics.title: C7.1 The characteristic properties of acids and bases

subtopics.title: C7.1 The characteristic properties of acids and bases

outcomes.text: Describe acid, base and alkali reactions, indicator colours, pH comparisons, and neutralisation producing salt and water.
Classify acidic, basic and amphoteric oxides, and describe amphoteric reactions with acids and bases.
Prepare, separate and purify soluble salts; define hydrated and anhydrous substances; and prepare insoluble salts by precipitation.
Describe Periodic Table periods, groups and atomic-number order, explain periodic trends and group similarities, and identify trends from data.
Describe Group I metals and trends in melting point, density and water reactivity, and predict properties of other members.
Describe halogen properties, appearances and trends, explain halogen displacement reactions, and predict properties of other Group VII elements.
Describe transition elements as dense, high-melting metals forming coloured compounds and commonly acting as catalysts.
Describe noble gases as unreactive, monatomic gases and explain their low reactivity using electronic configuration.
Compare metals and non-metals physically, and describe metal reactions with dilute acids, cold water and steam.
Relate aluminium and copper uses in aircraft, cables, food containers and wiring to density, conductivity and corrosion resistance.
Describe alloy composition, structure, representations, increased hardness and strength, and uses such as stainless-steel cutlery.
Use the reactivity series to predict metal reactions, displacement, and relative reactivity, and deduce an order from experimental results.
Explain rusting conditions, barrier methods, galvanising and sacrificial protection using reactivity and electron loss.
Relate extraction difficulty to reactivity, and describe iron extraction from hematite and aluminium extraction from bauxite.
Test for water and purity, explain distilled-water use, and describe domestic water treatment by sedimentation, filtration, carbon and chlorination.
State clean-air composition and identify sources of carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, particulates, methane, nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide.
Draw and interpret displayed formulas; distinguish saturated and unsaturated compounds; and describe homologous-series characteristics.
Name and draw displayed or structural formulas for specified simple organic compounds and identify compound types from names or formulas.
Identify fossil fuels and petroleum fractions, explain fractional distillation, state fraction uses, and describe trends in fraction properties.
Describe alkanes as saturated hydrocarbons with single covalent bonds and generally low reactivity apart from combustion.
Describe alkene structure, testing, cracking manufacture, and addition reactions with bromine, hydrogen and steam.
Describe complete ethanol combustion and state its uses as a solvent and fuel.
Define polymers, explain addition and condensation polymerisation, identify repeat units, deduce structures, and describe nylon.

units.title: C12 Experimental techniques and chemical analysis

outcomes.text: Select measurement apparatus and define solvents, solutes, solutions, saturated solutions, residues and filtrates.
Describe acid–base titrations using burettes, volumetric pipettes and indicators, including endpoint identification.
Use paper chromatography to separate coloured mixtures, interpret chromatograms, assess purity and calculate Rf values.
Explain and select suitable separation or purification methods, and use melting and boiling points to assess purity.

topics.title: C12.5 Identification of ions and gases

subtopics.title: C12.5 Identification of ions and gases

outcomes.text: Perform tests identifying specified anions, cations and gases, including flame tests for selected cations.

topics.title: P1.1 Physical quantities and measurement techniques

outcomes.text: Measure lengths, volumes and times, determine averages, and distinguish scalar quantities from vector quantities.
Define and calculate speed, velocity and acceleration; interpret motion graphs; and determine motion quantities from gradients and areas.

Explain qualitatively how centre-of-gravity position affects the stability of simple objects.

Recognise the Sun as the main energy source for most resources, excluding geothermal, nuclear and tidal energy.

Know that nuclear fission releases energy in nuclear reactors.
Define power as work done or energy transferred per unit time and use both equations.
Understand energy stores, transfers and conservation; calculate kinetic and gravitational energy, work, power and efficiency; compare energy resources and their environmental impacts.
Describe how pressure changes with force and area in everyday situations.
Define pressure as force per unit area and use p = F/A.
Explain how pressure depends on force and area, define pressure as force per unit area, and use p = F/A.
